description: The plot illustrates how GPU memory usage varies with the number of video frames for four models. The x-axis is labeled “Number of Frames,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 1000 with major tick labels at 0, 200, 400, 600, 800, and 1000. The y-axis is labeled “Memory (GB),” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 400 with major tick labels every 50 GB. Four solid lines with circular markers are shown: the gold line (VideoLLaMB-R) increases gradually from about 15 GB at 16 frames to about 38 GB at 1024 frames, passing through roughly 18 GB (128), 22 GB (256), and 28 GB (512); the green line (PLLaVA) rises from about 16 GB at 16 frames to about 76 GB at 1024 frames, with intermediate points near 22 GB (128), 30 GB (256), and 45 GB (512); the teal line (LLaVA-NeXT) increases from about 17 GB at 16 frames to about 145 GB at 1024 frames, with points around 28 GB (128), 45 GB (256), and 75 GB (512); the purple line (VideoLLAVA) increases steeply over the smaller frame counts shown, from about 22 GB at 16 frames to about 230 GB at 256 frames, with intermediate points near 30 GB (32), 40 GB (64), 68 GB (80), and 122 GB (128), and then continues upward beyond the plotted y-axis range after 256 frames.
